newsitem.title: UK: Physical copper trade seen rising as price drops.
newsitem.headline: Physical copper trade seen rising as price drops.

text.p: Physical copper business is expected to pick up as the cash metal price declines on the London Metal Exchange (LME, traders said.
But physical premiums are seen holding relatively steady despite a recent softening attributed to steady stock rises, they added.
"Premiums had faltered a bit and with the big back and high price people were not buying," a trader said. "But consumers would rather buy at this (lower) price, so merchants can keep premiums up."
Three months copper dropped about $100 from Tuesday on fund liquidation and further losses towards $2,200 were expected.
Meanwhile the cash to threes backwardation contracted about $20 to around $110/$120 after flaring in recent weeks on tightness in July.
"The lower prices will bring in more end-user buying, which means cathode buyers may do some fixing on their longer term contracts," said another trader.
"It will generally be pricing demand rather than metal demand, although lower prices may also attract fresh sales of cathode."
European premiums for Grade A copper ranged from around $10/$20 in Rotterdam to $35/$40 in the U.K., where business was reported at around $38, traders said.
